title: Socialism Is Dead! Long Live Socialism!: The Marx Code—Socialism with a Human Face
author: Vladimir A. Borisov
target_audience: Academics and students in political science and economics
Readers interested in Marxism and leftist theory
Progressives and socialists exploring alternative economic systems
Policymakers and activists analyzing contemporary socialism
core_themes: Evolution and failures of traditional socialism
Reinterpretation of Marx's ideas for the modern era
Comparison between socialism, capitalism, and mixed economies
Role of democracy and human rights in socialism
primary_purpose: To critically examine the shortcomings of 20th-century socialism, reinterpret Marxist theory in light of recent history, and propose a new, more human-centric form of socialism for the contemporary world.

structure_format.narrative_style: Analytical, argumentative, referencing historical and current examples
structure_format.organization: Structured in thematic chapters outlining socialism’s history, critique, and reconstruction; interspersed with commentary on global political developments
features: Comparative analysis of different socialist experiences

key_concepts_lessons: 20th-century socialism failed due to detachment from genuine Marxist principles and lack of democratic practice.
Classical Marxism can be revived by adapting its core tenets to respect individual freedoms and human rights.
Contemporary socialism must combine economic justice with democratic governance (‘socialism with a human face’).
Dogmatism and authoritarianism undermine socialist ideals.
Societal and economic models need to evolve with technological progress and changing social dynamics.
notable_features: Coining or promoting the idea of 'The Marx Code'—a modern blueprint for socialism
Addresses both historical analysis and policy recommendations
Integrates sociological and economic analysis with philosophical reflection
Seeks reconciliation between socialist ethics and individual liberties
cultural_historical_context: Published three decades after the fall of the Soviet bloc and amidst renewed debate over socialism in the 21st century, the book responds to global dissatisfaction with both neoliberal capitalism and traditional state socialism.
reception_impact: Appreciated by readers seeking a balanced critique of past socialist systems
Utilized as a reference in progressive academic discussions
Generates debate over how to modernize Marxist theory while retaining its social justice roots
Not widely mainstream but circulates in scholarly and activist circles
comparable_titles: Socialism...Seriously: A Brief Guide to Human Liberation by Danny Katch
Why You Should Be a Socialist by Nathan J. Robinson
The ABCs of Socialism edited by Bhaskar Sunkara
Chavismo and the End of the Venezuelan Dream by Cristina Marcano
